post.description: Creates a monitor through the same path as the dashboard wizard: product-default criteria (going offline auto-declares an incident that auto-resolves on recovery), initial Operational state, plan limits enforced. Website/API/External Status Page take `url`; Ping/IP/Port/DNS/SSL Certificate/Domain take `host`; Manual and Incoming Request/Email take no target. Synthetic/script, SNMP and Server monitors must be created in the dashboard. Send an `Idempotency-Key` header to make retries safe.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key

schema.description: Optional client-generated key (1-255 visible ASCII characters; a UUID works) making this POST safely retryable. Retrying with the SAME key and byte-identical body within 24h replays the stored first response. The same key with a different body answers 422 `idempotency_key_reused`; a retry racing the first execution answers 409 `idempotency_in_progress`. Omitting the header executes normally with no idempotency guarantee.

patch.description: Changes one or more of a monitor's editable fields through the same domain path as the dashboard's own edit forms. Every field is optional; omitted fields are left untouched, and `description` accepts null to clear it. `url` applies to Website/API/External Status Page monitors and `host` to Ping/IP/Port/DNS/SSL Certificate/Domain monitors — the one the monitor's type does not use is refused rather than silently ignored. `request_timeout_seconds` is a Website/API setting (null restores the 30-second default), and `failure_threshold` is refused for Manual, Incoming Request and Incoming Email monitors. `heartbeat_interval_minutes` and `heartbeat_grace_minutes` set the dead-man's-switch schedule of an Incoming Request monitor — how long silence may last before it is declared down — and are refused for every other type. At least one field must be present.

schema.description: Monitor id.

parameters.description: Monitor id.

url.description: New target URL (Website, API, External Status Page monitors).

host.description: New target hostname or IP (Ping, IP, Port, DNS, SSL Certificate, Domain monitors).

request_timeout_seconds.description: Per-request probe timeout in seconds (1-60, Website and API monitors). Null restores the 30-second default.

failure_threshold.description: Consecutive failed checks required before this monitor declares an incident or alert (1-10). Refused for Manual, Incoming Request and Incoming Email monitors, which have no run of failed checks to count.

heartbeat_interval_minutes.description: How often the job watching this monitor promises to ping it, in minutes (1-10080). Incoming Request monitors only — refused for every other type.

heartbeat_grace_minutes.description: Extra minutes a late ping is allowed before the monitor is declared down (0-10080). 0 declares the moment a ping is late. Incoming Request monitors only.

schema.description: At least one field is required — an empty object is refused.

MonitorConfig.description: A project's monitors as portable, versioned configuration. Contains no ids, secrets, incidents or status history.

name.description: Monitor display name. Together with `monitor_type` this is the identity an import de-duplicates on — there is no portable id. Leading and trailing whitespace is trimmed; a name that is only whitespace is refused.

monitor_type.description: Monitor protocol type, e.g. "Website", "API", "Ping", "Port", "DNS", "SSL Certificate", "Domain", "Incoming Request".

url.description: Target URL for URL-checked types (Website, API, External Status Page, Synthetic Monitor, Custom JavaScript Code).

host.description: Target hostname or IP for host-checked types (Ping, IP, Port, DNS, SSL Certificate, Domain, SNMP).

dns_record_type.description: DNS record type for DNS monitors.

monitoring_interval.description: Cron-shaped check cadence. Null means the type has no outbound probe cadence (Manual, Incoming Request, Incoming Email).

request_timeout_seconds.description: Per-request probe timeout in seconds (Website and API monitors). Absent means the 30-second default.

failure_threshold.description: Consecutive failed checks required before this monitor declares an incident or alert.

heartbeat_interval_minutes.description: How often the job watching an Incoming Request monitor promises to ping it, in minutes.

heartbeat_grace_minutes.description: Extra minutes a late heartbeat ping is allowed before the monitor is declared down.

labels.description: Label NAMES, not ids — a label id means nothing in another project. On import, names matching the destination project's existing labels are attached; names it does not have are reported back rather than created.

has_more.description: True when another page exists after this one.

next_cursor.description: Opaque cursor for the next page (pass as `after`); null on the last page.

MonitorList.description: One page of the project's monitors.

active_monitoring_disabled.description: True when active probing is switched off for this monitor (manually or by maintenance).

failure_threshold.description: How many consecutive failed checks this monitor must record before it declares an incident or alert. 1 alerts on the first failed check. Honoured for monitor types an outbound probe checks and for Server monitors (each overdue or over-limit report is one failed check); a short blip below the threshold still appears on the timeline and status pages, it just does not page anyone.

Monitor.description: A monitor and its current status.

color.description: Display color of the status (hex), when configured.

type.description: URI identifying the problem class; resolves to its docs page.

title.description: Short human-readable summary of the problem class. Never parse it — switch on `code`.

status.description: HTTP status code, duplicated from the response.

detail.description: Human-readable explanation specific to this occurrence.

code.description: Stable machine-readable problem code — the value SDKs branch on.

request_id.description: The x-request-id of the failing request — quote it in support requests.

pointer.description: RFC 6901 JSON Pointer to the offending request field.

deleted.description: Always true — the monitor is gone from every surface.

monitor.description: The monitor the history belongs to.

starts_at.description: When the monitor entered this status.

ends_at.description: When the status ended; null while it is still current.

root_cause.description: Recorded cause of the transition, when available.

alerts_muted_until.description: When the mute expires, ISO-8601 UTC; null when the monitor is not muted.

dry_run.description: True when nothing was written and the counts describe what an apply WOULD do.

created_count.description: Monitors created — or, in a dry run, the number that would be.

skipped_count.description: Entries skipped because a live monitor already has that name and type.

invalid_count.description: Entries that cannot describe a monitor.

failed_count.description: Entries whose creation was attempted and errored. Always 0 in a dry run.

unmatched_labels.description: Label names the document referenced that this project does not have. They are reported, never created — inventing labels during an import would quietly reshape the destination project's taxonomy.

StatusPageResource.description: One monitor shown on a status page.

deleted.description: Always true — the row is off the page.

StatusPageResourceDetached.description: A resource removed from a status page.

data.description: One entry per on-call schedule in the project.

OnCallCurrent.description: Live on-call rosters for every schedule.

current_user.description: Who is on call right now; null when nobody is.

next_user.description: Who takes over next; null when unknown.

handoff_at.description: When the current roster hands off, ISO-8601 UTC.

next_start_at.description: When the next roster begins, ISO-8601 UTC.

OnCallScheduleRoster.description: The live roster of one on-call schedule.

OnCallUserRef.description: A user on an on-call roster.

period_start.description: Start of the current UTC calendar-month period.

period_end.description: When the monthly allowance resets, ISO-8601 UTC.

Usage.description: The project's API allowances and current consumption.

has_more.description: True when another page exists after this one.

next_cursor.description: Opaque cursor for the next page (pass as `after`); null on the last page.

WebhookEndpointList.description: One page of the project's webhook endpoints.

url.description: The https:// URL deliveries are POSTed to.

event_types.description: Event types this endpoint is subscribed to.

enabled.description: False when paused by you, or auto-disabled after sustained delivery failures (see `disabled_reason`).

disabled_reason.description: Why the endpoint was automatically disabled, when it was. Null otherwise.

consecutive_failures.description: Deliveries that failed terminally in a row. Resets to 0 on any success.

secret_hint.description: Last 4 characters of the signing secret — enough to identify it, useless as a key. The full secret is shown only at create and rotate time.

secret.description: The signing secret (`whsec_…`). SHOWN ONCE — it is never retrievable again. Store it before you discard this response.

WebhookEndpointCreated.description: A newly created endpoint and its one-time signing secret.

WebhookEndpointDeleted.description: Confirmation that the endpoint was removed.

secret.description: The NEW signing secret (`whsec_…`). Shown once.

previous_secret_expires_at.description: Until this moment BOTH the previous and the new secret sign every delivery (two `v1,…` entries in one `webhook-signature` header), so you can roll your verifier without dropping an event.

WebhookSecretRotated.description: A rotated signing secret and its overlap window.

has_more.description: True when another page exists after this one.

next_cursor.description: Opaque cursor for the next page (pass as `after`); null on the last page.

WebhookDeliveryList.description: Recent deliveries for one endpoint, newest first.

webhook_event_id.description: The value sent in the `webhook-id` header — stable across retries, and the dedup key on your side.

response_status.description: HTTP status your endpoint answered, when it answered.

error.description: Why the last attempt failed, in plain language.

WebhookDelivery.description: One delivery attempt-chain for a single event.

version.description: Document format version. A file carrying a higher version is refused rather than partially understood.

monitors.description: The monitors, sorted by name so the document is diffable. At most 500 per document — a larger fleet imports in batches.

MonitorConfigOutput.description: A project's monitors as portable, versioned configuration. Contains no ids, secrets, incidents or status history.

name.description: Monitor display name. Together with `monitor_type` this is the identity an import de-duplicates on — there is no portable id. Leading and trailing whitespace is trimmed; a name that is only whitespace is refused.

monitor_type.description: Monitor protocol type, e.g. "Website", "API", "Ping", "Port", "DNS", "SSL Certificate", "Domain", "Incoming Request".

url.description: Target URL for URL-checked types (Website, API, External Status Page, Synthetic Monitor, Custom JavaScript Code).

host.description: Target hostname or IP for host-checked types (Ping, IP, Port, DNS, SSL Certificate, Domain, SNMP).

dns_record_type.description: DNS record type for DNS monitors.

monitoring_interval.description: Cron-shaped check cadence. Null means the type has no outbound probe cadence (Manual, Incoming Request, Incoming Email).

request_timeout_seconds.description: Per-request probe timeout in seconds (Website and API monitors). Absent means the 30-second default.

failure_threshold.description: Consecutive failed checks required before this monitor declares an incident or alert.

heartbeat_interval_minutes.description: How often the job watching an Incoming Request monitor promises to ping it, in minutes.

heartbeat_grace_minutes.description: Extra minutes a late heartbeat ping is allowed before the monitor is declared down.

labels.description: Label NAMES, not ids — a label id means nothing in another project. On import, names matching the destination project's existing labels are attached; names it does not have are reported back rather than created.

bearerAuth.description: An `uptimely_live_` project API key (Settings → API Keys).
